S53.02.needs: at least one installed or created skill
S53.02.note: The cited commandSetup.ts:2309 and surfaces/index.ts:382 quotes are gone; the list is built in capabilityManagement.ts (manageSkills) and settingsWebviewContent.ts.
steps: Click Settings in the app, then click Skills in the left list.
Read the Loaded skills list: each row shows a skill name and its description.
Or open the Command Palette and type Code: Show Skills to open the full list.
Compare with Expected: the skills installed or made for you should appear in the list.
S53.02.where: Settings > Skills > Loaded skills (full list: Settings > Skills > Manage skills, or Command Palette > Code: Show Skills)

S53.03.note: The list shows the raw scope word user, not Personal; the personal folder path comes from code, not a run.
steps: Click Settings, then Skills, then click Manage skills.
Click Create a skill and choose Personal.
Type a lowercase name with hyphens, such as release-notes, and a description, following the prompts.
The new skill file opens for editing. Check it saved under ~/.agiworkforce/skills (or AGIWORKFORCE_HOME if set), and that the list shows its scope as user.
Compare with Expected: the skill is yours and is not tied to one folder.
S53.03.where: Settings > Skills > Manage skills > Create a skill > Personal

S53.04.needs: a project folder open in VS Code
S53.04.note: The project folder is <workspace>/.agiworkforce/skills per skillAuthoring.ts; the check in the other folder is inferred from that path, not run. The quoted capabilityManagement.ts:101 line is gone.
steps: Open a project folder in VS Code.
Click Settings, then Skills, then Manage skills.
Click Create a skill, choose This project, and name the skill.
Check the list: the new skill shows scope project and not allowed yet until you allow it.
Click Allow this folder’s project skills, then open another folder and check the skill does not appear there.
Compare with Expected: the skill loads only in the project it was made for.
S53.04.where: Settings > Skills > Manage skills > Create a skill > This project

S53.07.needs: at least one installed or created skill
S53.07.note: A skill not yet allowed in this folder shows Not allowed in this folder yet in place of its description (capabilityManagement.ts).
steps: Click Settings, then Skills.
Look at each row in Loaded skills: the skill name is the title and its description is shown under it.
Open Command Palette, type Code: Show Skills, and check each entry shows the name, description and scope.
Compare with Expected: each skill shows its name and what it does.
S53.07.where: Settings > Skills > Loaded skills (also Command Palette > Code: Show Skills)

S53.10.note: Code shows the skill's bundled files are listed under its folder for the model (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:1218); that the model reads them was not confirmed by reading code.
steps: Create a skill (Settings > Skills > Manage skills > Create a skill > Personal).
In its folder, next to SKILL.md, add a references folder with a text file that holds a made-up fact.
Make sure the skill is on, then in the chat ask a question that needs that fact and asks for the skill to be used.
Compare with Expected: the answer uses the fact from the reference file.
S53.10.where: Inside a skill run, seen in the chat answer

S53.11.note: apps/cli/src/skills.rs hashes the scripts folder and lists it for the model (line 1218), but no code found that runs scripts automatically; that whether they run is unknown.
steps: Create a skill and add a scripts folder with a small script that writes a marker file.
In SKILL.md, tell the model to run that script.
Make sure the skill is on, then in the chat ask for the task the skill covers.
Compare with Expected: the script runs and the marker file appears.
S53.11.where: Inside a skill run, seen in the chat answer or a command the chat runs

S53.14.needs: a skill that lists required tools, such as one you write
S53.14.note: The Loaded skills rows show only the description; the requirement line appears only in the Manage skills list.
steps: Click Settings, then Skills, then Manage skills.
Find a skill whose SKILL.md lists a tool it needs, or create one that names a tool.
Read the detail after its description: it shows Needs followed by the tool names.
Compare with Expected: a skill whose tool is missing shows Missing ... so it will not load, and does not load.
S53.14.where: Settings > Skills > Manage skills (read the detail line of a skill row)

S53.17.needs: a skill that is on and allowed in this folder
S53.17.note: The start-screen group lists only skills that are on and allowed (startSuggestions.ts); the conditions for showing the start screen were not checked, and the /skills slash entry opens the manager, not a picker for a message.
steps: Open the chat and start a new chat so the start screen shows.
Under the Skills heading, click a skill name; the message box fills with Use the <name> skill to.
Type the task after it and send.
Compare with Expected: the reply follows that skill.
S53.17.where: Chat start screen > Skills (group) > click the skill name

S53.18.needs: a skill that is on and allowed
S53.18.note: The skill catalog is placed in the model prompt (apps/cli/src/agent/prompt.rs and apps/cli/src/skills.rs format_skill_catalog_for_prompt); the choice is made by the model, so the cited quote is gone and it is not a code rule. The description-matching itself was not run.
steps: Create a skill with a clear description, such as one about writing release notes.
Make sure it is on and allowed (Settings > Skills > Loaded skills).
In the chat, ask for a task that matches the description without naming the skill.
Compare with Expected: the reply follows the skill's steps.
S53.18.where: Inside a chat request; seen in the chat answer

S53.20.needs: a skill that is allowed in this folder (the switch is disabled otherwise)
S53.20.note: Removing a personal skill is a different action and deletes its folder; it is not part of this check.
steps: Click Settings, then Skills.
In Loaded skills, flip the switch of a skill to off; the status line shows Turning <name> off.
Click Manage skills and check the row now shows the off icon.
Flip it back on, and check the skill is still listed (it was not deleted).
S53.20.where: Settings > Skills > Loaded skills (switch on each row), or Settings > Skills > Manage skills > the skill row's Turn off / Turn on button
